clue.text: Foolish daughter's at the back of the boat when sailor's taking charge

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

blocks.clueFragment: at the back of the boat
blocks.note: the rear part of a vessel is its stern end, described with this nautical word
as in 'as I arrived', meaning at the time that
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
to charge at someone is to rush at them

explanation.surface: A silly daughter lounges at the stern while a sailor takes command of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The "'s" after daughter is just the surface's grammar; 'when' gives a short conjunction, not a time word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft as a brush is a British idiom for someone very silly or scatterbrained.

clue.text: Diversion during last month takes junction out of use

indicators.note: during means within the span of a period, so one piece sits inside the other
takes means adds on, so a further piece is attached at the end

blocks.note: December is the final month of the year, abbreviated
a diversion is an amusement or bit of fun
a T-junction is named after the letter's shape

explanation.surface: A road diversion through December closes off a junction so nobody can use it.
explanation.walkthrough: The junction is a T-junction, so its letter is the one shaped like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct no longer works or exists, just as equipment out of use has stopped functioning.

clue.text: Stroked female working dog's head and took control

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of dog is used

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
a machine that is working is switched on
the opening letter of dog
to take control is to lead, here in the past tense

explanation.surface: A woman petted her working dog's head and then took charge of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fondle is to caress or stroke lovingly, and both verbs here are past tense.

clue.text: Staggered by scrum following One Direction

indicators.note: one thing following another means it is placed after it in the line of letters

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
a compass point
a ruck is a scrum-like loose melee in rugby, and a scrum of people is a ruck

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at being caught in a crush of fans following the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: A + WEST + RUCK. One Direction was a British boy band, which hides that the words must be taken separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To be staggered is to be astonished, and an awestruck person is filled with amazed wonder.

clue.text: Pretended to throw out cadet

indicators.note: to throw something out of order jumbles it, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feigned an attempt to expel a young officer trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to put on a performance, so someone who acted was only pretending.

clue.text: Knock about with bruiser at university

blocks.note: a rough is a violent person, a thug or bruiser
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A tough guy at college gets into fights.
explanation.walkthrough: Being up (at Oxford or Cambridge) is a British convention for being in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To rough someone up is to beat them or knock them about physically.

clue.text: Drinks bottle's last dregs

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the tail of dregs is used

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, which is spirit
the final letter of dregs

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off the last dregs in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, so it gives SPIRIT, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are strong distilled alcoholic drinks such as whisky, gin or vodka.

clue.text: Visits very good English church on Sunday that is falling apart

blocks.note: someone who visits a place goes to it
pi is short for pious, a crossword sense of very good
E is the abbreviation for English
CE is the Church of England
S is the abbreviation for Sunday, placed after the rest

explanation.surface: A churchgoer visits a fine old English church on Sunday, only to find it crumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: GOES TO + PI + E + CE + S. 'Very good' looks like TOP, but the TO already comes with visits; very good is PI.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pieces is an idiom for losing composure or collapsing, much like falling apart.

clue.text: Wrongdoing connected with East Anglian church?

blocks.note: of expresses a connection, as in 'the people of the town'
the Fens are low marshy lands of East Anglia in England
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A query whether some misdeed involves a church in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: OF + FEN + CE. The Fens are flat marshland in East Anglia, the eastern bulge of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a crime or breach of a rule, which is a form of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Organisation of travel to old city's mismanaged

indicators.note: the word splits as mis plus managed, and letters that are badly managed end up out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
the first three letters of mismanaged, taken as they stand

explanation.surface: Holiday trips to an ancient city are badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: Mismanaged has to be read as two parts, MIS and managed, the second working on the first: TO + UR + ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism is the business of arranging holidays, travel and visits for tourists.

clue.text: Tortuous drive meant us having accident

indicators.note: a tortuous route twists and turns, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A winding, twisty drive led to the group crashing the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is a mishap or unlucky accident; death by misadventure is a coroner's verdict for accidental death.

clue.text: Awkwardly silent about guy, initially appearing in underwear

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap round another piece
initially points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of guy

explanation.surface: An awkward, silent man is caught in his underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn as an undergarment, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Writer spoke briefly about flowers

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of spoke's synonym is dropped
about can mean turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards

blocks.note: Roald Dahl, the children's author
spoke and said are both past tenses of speaking

explanation.surface: An author talked briefly about flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the dahlia really is named after a man called Dahl, the Swedish botanist Anders Dahl.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are showy garden plants with large many-petalled blooms, so they are flowers.

clue.text: Chose to adopt editorial content

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies inside it, so the answer sits within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: found inside these two words, across the gap

explanation.surface: An editor decided to take on a piece of opinion writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across adOPT EDitorial.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose or decide, and both verbs here are in the past tense.

clue.text: Nobody's against multinational organisation having work arranged

blocks.note: the United Nations
op, short for opus, is a musical work
to pose a group for a photograph is to arrange it

explanation.surface: No one objects to the United Nations organising a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: if nobody is against a proposal, it is unopposed.
explanation.definitionFit: An unopposed candidate or motion faces no opposition, which is exactly the state of nobody being against it.

clue.text: Not in area by 1st July, old boy becomes unemployed

indicators.note: 1st means first, so only the opening letter of the month's name is used

blocks.note: not inside something is out of it
A is the abbreviation for area
the opening letter of July
OB is short for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil who has left the district by the start of July finds himself jobless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' only joins the pieces. Old boy, OB, is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of a job has no work, the plain meaning of unemployed.

clue.text: Kill male rabbit and get regular meat for cooler

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter of meat is taken

blocks.note: ice is underworld slang for kill
a buck is a male rabbit, hare or deer
the second and fourth letters of meat

explanation.surface: A grim recipe: slaughter a buck rabbit and take some meat for the cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE as kill is gangster slang, and only the even letters of meat are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bucket is a container of ice used to keep bottles of wine or champagne chilled, a kind of cooler.

clue.text: Hesitation about ridiculous quota with zero latitude

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the hesitation wraps round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over an absurd quota that allows no leeway at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero latitude' reads as no freedom; it is the definition, meaning the line at 0 degrees of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary circle round the Earth from which latitude is measured, at 0 degrees.

clue.text: Many met up going out with bridge players

indicators.note: going out suggests leaving the usual arrangement, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
East and North are two of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Lots of people got together on a night out with their bridge partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, so any two of N, E, S, W can be bridge players.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for an indefinitely large number, meaning very many.

clue.text: Place religious education with priest

blocks.note: a pad is informal for one's home or place
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A school's RE lessons are put in the hands of a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain in the armed forces, or informally any priest or clergyman.

clue.text: Some rampant algae can appear to be a cure-all

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the phrase
rampant means rearing up, and in a down clue rising letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a run of letters across these words: algAE CAN APpear

explanation.surface: Spreading algae might seem to be a miracle remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' looks like a description of the algae, but it is the signal to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a remedy supposed to cure every disease or solve every problem.

clue.text: Sketched funny old journalist supporting party

indicators.note: funny means odd or strange, so the following letters are put in a strange order
in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits beneath it in the column

blocks.note: a do is an informal party
taken as written
ed is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An amusing veteran reporter drew cartoons for a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to draw idly, so the past tense doodled describes having sketched aimlessly.

clue.text: Charlie's funny dog, maybe, has teatime treat

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rum is a British word for odd or funny
a dog is one example of a pet

explanation.surface: Charlie's comical dog gets something tasty at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a soft griddle cake with holes, toasted and buttered in Britain at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpets are a traditional British snack eaten hot with butter at afternoon tea.

clue.text: Boxer beginning to train young lad

indicators.note: beginning to two words means taking only the start of each

blocks.note: the opening letter of train
the opening letter of young
a son is a male child or lad

explanation.surface: A boxer starts coaching a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer beginning to train' reads as one picture, but the beginnings belong to both train and young.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson and Tyson Fury are famous heavyweight champions, so the surname suits a boxer.

clue.text: Detect slight mistrust in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the words are judged by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: slight is fine, as in a fine distinction, and mistrust is doubt

explanation.surface: Someone senses a faint suspicion while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out is to discover or learn something, which is what it means to detect it.

clue.text: My dogs?

blocks.note: surface: someone asking about their own pet dogs, perhaps a breed of gun dog
'my' is the voice of the crossword compiler, and the breed of dog shares its name with the people who compile puzzles

explanation.walkthrough: The breed of gun dog shares its name with crossword compilers, and 'my' is the compiler speaking of their own kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters are a breed of gun dog, and also the people who compile crosswords, the setter's own colleagues.

clue.text: Good-humoured old copper's put on line in clash

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the combined pieces sit within the clash

blocks.note: to jar is to clash, as colours or sounds can
O is the abbreviation for old
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A cheerful retired policeman is put on the line in a confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper here is the metal's chemical symbol, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular means joking or humorous, so a good-humoured person is jocular.

clue.text: Platform for pressing items?

blocks.note: surface: a stage for urgent matters, as in an agenda of pressing business
setter's reading: a flat surface on which clothes are pressed with a hot iron

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suggests urgent, but it means flattening clothes with heat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironing board is the padded, folding stand on which garments are laid to be pressed smooth.
